notes.title: Ladder it Up! - "Ascend" Update
notes.notes:
And here we go, big update just landed!
This section is divided into two parts: Patch Notes and Final Thoughts & Plans for 2025.

[b][h1]Patch Notes:[/h1][/b]
[list]
[*] Controller Support Added
[i](You still need mouse to use pause menu and main menu)[/i]
[*] Added contextual animations for specific actions: ladder preparation, ladder spawn, ladder pickup, and crystal collection
[i]Animations can be disabled by unchecking the "Contextual Animations" box[/i]
[*] Added a "Controls" button in the pause menu (Displays keybinds only, no remapping, sorry)
[*] Added a new ladder as a reward for completing the bonus level
[*] Added a festive holiday ladder 
[i](It will remain unlockable after the holiday season but will be relocated)[/i]
[*] You can now check the description of game modes by clicking on the mode's sign in the main menu
[*] Added a warning before exiting the game
[*] Removed the "EXIT" button from the pause menu
[*] Added an option to disable motion blur
[*] Introduced a new bonus level: Ascent, unlocked after completing the game on Normal mode
[*] Added a mute button in the main menu to silence the bird loop 
[i](Click the bird icon at the top)[/i]
[*] Fixed shadow noise 
[i](I guess?)[/i]
[*] Added a holiday hat for Gustaw (the player character) during the holiday season.
[*] Added stun sound effects and VFX
[*] Adjusted ladder spawn positions 
[i](Let me know how it feels!)[/i]
[*] Improved lighting in various areas
[*] Fixed several geometry issues
[*] Slightly increased the jump height of the character
[*] Revamped the main menu
[*] And probably some other changes I’ve already forgotten about lol
[/list]

[h1]New Mechanics in "Ascent" Bonus Level[/h1]
The Ascent level introduces new mechanics that weren’t present in previous levels:

[list]
[*] Speed Boost 
[i]Collecting it temporarily turns your character blue and increases movement speed[/i]
[*] Jump Platforms
[i]Green platforms that launch the player upward upon contact[/i]
[*] Weak Wooden Platforms 
[i]Unlike purple platforms that function similarly, these collapse instantly[/i]
[*] Trap Doors
[*] Windmills
[*] Arrow Wall and Ceiling Trap
[/list]

[h1]Final Thoughts & Plans for 2025:[/h1]
Ladder It Up was undoubtedly an interesting adventure for me as a solo dev, and it helped me better understand the various challenges one can face as a game developer. While it wasn’t my dream game, it taught me a lot—especially the importance of focusing on games I’m truly passionate about and excited to create. That’s exactly what you can expect from me in the coming year.

As I mentioned in my previous post, I don’t plan to actively work on Ladder It Up and would like to focus on my next projects, HOWEVER, if you have any suggestions or ideas related to the game [b]especially[/b] if you come across any bugs, feel free to post in the Steam discussions, leave a review, or join the Discord server: https://discord.gg/AsFdUh85cR , and I’ll do my best to address your needs.

My goal for 2025 is to release a FPS Single Player game in early access, inspired by games like XIII, GoldenEye 007, The Operative: No One Lives Forever, and TimeSplitters. Will it work? Time will tell. My main goal is to deliver the best possible FPS that I can make, that focuses on variety and humor, not just to evoke a sense of nostalgia, but also to prove that FPS games aren’t limited to just Call of Duty and boomer shooters. I want to create a game that I’ll genuinely enjoy playing myself, and a type of game that I feel is currently missing in the market. Alright, maybe I’ll also come up with a small side project along the way, but it will definitely be within a genre I’m confident about.

Thanks to everyone for your support and for giving Ladder It Up a shot! As I mentioned, if you have any feedback, I’ll definitely take it into account. And now, Merry Christmas and Happy New Year!

notes.title: Your feedback is needed! Last Major Update in works!
notes.notes:
Hello everyone,
Ladder it Up is not definitively abandoned despite the lack of updates recently. I'm working on the final update, which will include new content, some fixes, and more. So if there's anything you'd like to see in the game, feel is missing, or if you simply have any suggestions, please share them on the Steam forum or join the Discord and post here: https://discord.gg/AsFdUh85cR 

There's no set date for the update yet, but I think there's a chance it might be released before the winter sale. The new map, along with the ASCEND mode, will bring a typical climbing game experience, with the addition of new mechanics as well as those you've encountered so far. The level is still in development. It won't be very long, but I believe it will offer a good amount of fun and new challenges. There are a few more things I want to introduce, but I'll wait to announce them until they're ready.

Here are some screenshots:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/dfe069df5e22d3592ee63b3f7cc9a7cb6f3d69e2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/3093eb3ebd6f526f5d865059668de2834f4369c6.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/709e25e6bde64024ab75401293048d1caac50fc2.png[/img]

Additionally, due to the lack of further support after the update (except for necessary fixes or patches), the price of Ladder It Up will be permanently reduced a bit in certain regions. This price change will occur with the next major update, and the game will also be regularly available on Steam sales.

And now for the Q&A segment:

[b]"Why the end?"[/b]
From the beginning, I envisioned Ladder It Up as a quick and short project that would allow me to develop other titles. I’m also a proponent of buying a game and having it in an almost unchanged form, rather than watching it evolve so much that it stops being what I initially liked about it. What's more, I wouldn’t want to be tied down to working on just one game for the next few years. I prefer to grow as a developer by creating new games across different genres, being able to look at each title and know what I learned while working on specific game.

[b]"What’s next since this is the end?"[/b]
I'm still working on new games and have plenty of ideas. So, Ladder It Up is just the beginning, and it was mainly created with the goal of funding the next projects.

It was also an important lesson in game development due to a few missteps, shortcomings, and feedback that will help me avoid repeating the same mistakes in the future, especially in terms of game marketing.

[b]"What are the next games"[/b]
I’m currently working on two projects. 

One is a retro-style horror game that is in a very early stage of production, but I know it will take less time to complete. It will be a rather surreal horror game, focusing more on gameplay variety rather than a constantly unfolding story. The narrative will have more of a subliminal message than direct storytelling.

The main project (the one Ladder It Up was created to help fund), tentatively titled "Classic Shooter," is an FPS PvP game that offers interactive environments, clear and intuitive gameplay, and leans heavily into old-school vibes, similar to games like CS 1.6. Don't worry, I’m not aiming for it to be another competitive shooter, as my focus is more on fun rather than competition. That said, I aim to make the design as fair as possible, and if players want to organize tournaments, I’ll be happy to support that.

[b]“Where can I see the progress or support the projects?”[/b]
You can follow the progress on Classic Shooter or any other game I'll be working on, on my Twitter account: https://x.com/V0X3L1 or on my Ko-Fi profile: https://ko-fi.com/voxel_ld, where you can also support the projects through donations that will directly contribute to further development (assets, freelance commissions, etc.).

Thank you to everyone who purchased Ladder It Up, your support means a lot to me, and I hope you'll also be satisfied with the titles I release or work on in the future.

notes.title: Ladder It Up! - Major Update #7 | Movement improved, New features and much more!
notes.notes:
And here it is! A significant update focusing primarily on improving character movement, enhancing gameplay experience, and implementing many quality-of-life changes with newcomers in mind, along with content adjustments!

Here’s the list of changes:

[h2]New:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added climbing animation. Can be disabled in the options.
[*] Added an option for faster character rotation. Can be enabled in the options.
[*] Added guide lines showing where the bottom and top parts of the ladder will land upon spawning. Can be disabled in the options.
[*] Added an option to rotate the ladder along the X-axis. LMB + Scroll up or down.
[*] Added a sound effect when collecting crystals.
[*] Added a button in the main menu for synchronizing ladders based on unlocked Steam achievements.
[*] Added sounds and text notifications for each new location the player enters (available only on Normal).
[/list]

[h2]Movement:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Significantly improved geometry across all difficulty levels. It’s now more obvious whether a player can jump onto an obstacle or not.
[*] Animation and perspective now better reflect the height of the character’s jump.
[*] During a jump, the player's collision capsule temporarily shrinks to make it easier to jump onto obstacles.
[*] Slightly increased jump height.
[/list]

[h2]Levels:[/h2]

[h3]Easy:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Added ladder restocks on every level.
[/list]

[h3]Normal:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Glacial Path is now much harder.
[*] Added ladder restocks in several locations.
[*] Added a checkpoint and ladder restock near the lava ruined bridge.
[*] Moved the ladder restock near the volcano to the volcano cave, right by the checkpoint.
[*] Added a lantern by the ladder restock in the volcano.
[*] Changed the penultimate path in the volcano.
[*] Added new boulder spawn points on the penultimate path in the volcano.
[*] Added Icicles at Glacial Path... they don’t do anything, just look cool.
[/list]

[h3]Hard:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved lighting.
[*] Replaced falling boulders in the Stone Pit with moving walls.
[*] Removed falling boulders in the volcano after the one-way walls.
[*] Increased the distance a player travels when hit by Fire Boulders.
[*] Fire Boulders no longer require a specific velocity to stun the player.
[*] Fire Boulders have a fixed spawn time.
[/list]

[h2]Other fixes, improvements, and changes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Repositioned buttons in the menu.
[*] Changed the behavior of floating islands. They will now always pause for a moment when reaching a designated point.
[*] Fixed the text on the TimePortal machine. It now lights up.
[*] Added invisible blockers for boulders so they don’t leave their designated area.
[*] Boulders have a new shape and now move much faster.
[*] The arrows for selecting a ladder and game mode will disappear when the selection reaches the limit.
[*] Reduced the size of the Ice Ladder restock.
[*] When you’re smaller, you move faster.
[*] Adjusted jump height when you’re smaller so you can still clear the same obstacles.
[*] Improved the Steam page: new graphics, images, gifs, and a refreshed trailer.

[/list]

But that’s not all!

The game will be on sale at 50% off for this week only, from August 12th to August 19th (19 CEST). So if you know someone who thinks the base price is too high, feel free to suggest grabbing the game at discount!

And last but not least, we now have a Discord server! I understand that many people prefer other platforms over Steam discussions, so I’ve set up a server where I’ll be sharing updates, gathering your feedback, and keeping you informed about my work on other games.

Discord Link: https://discord.gg/AsFdUh85cR
X Link: https://x.com/V0X3L1

[/list]

notes.title: UPDATE #4 - First Major Update
notes.notes:
So, here's the first major update for Ladder It Up (likely one of two), which, in addition to further balance and QoL changes, includes a rework of a specific part of the map: the bridge.

Patch notes:

[list]
[h3]Boulders changes:[/h3]
[*] Increased the speed required for boulders to push the player
[*] Boulders that hit the player will break
[*] Boulders will push the player further and higher
[*] After being hit by a Boulder, the player is immune to another hit for a moment
[*] Boulders can destroy the ladder

[h3]Other changes[/h3]
[*] Added the ability to change the over-the-shoulder camera
[*] Improved the weight of plank ladder
[*] Enhanced the ladder spawn zone
[*] Changed the location of the Elder Gods summoning
[*] Made easy mode even easier
[*] Added arrows for selecting game modes
[*] Minor changes to the hard difficulty level
[*] Bridge part has been reworked
[/list]

[h3]Bridge:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/6339e6fecab4822aa997dc51bb20c1e6fb4a7976.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/067faca3505eeb5b0687a9c25a7c974f1e06a4f5.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/f8db6014e70e237bb7926421cc9683b4e23215da.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45038219/08623e68f5bf35a6adc12833bd022fe546473456.png[/img]

You might be asking: "WHYYYYYY?!"
While playing, I noticed several problems with the first version. First, you encounter the new "flying islands" mechanic and immediately risk losing a significant amount of progress. That sucks. So, I've adjusted the first part of the bridge to give you space to test, check out, and learn how the "flying islands" work in peace.

Another issue I noticed in both parts featuring "flying islands" is the practical lack of ladder use. What's the point of Ladder It Up if you don't need to use the ladder and you're moving downward?

Now, at the cost of an easier introduction, I've increased the difficulty in the second part of the bridge. Enjoy your [strike]suffering [/strike] climbing!

notes.title: Ladder It Up #2 - Quicker Ladder pick up, Ladder spawn cancel, Camera Changes
notes.notes:
There will be one more update before I leave. This update contains some Quality of Life changes, as follows:
[list]
[*][h3] Reduced time needed to pick up the ladder after spawning: 1.45 -> 1.3 [/h3]
It should help you keep the flow.
[*][h3]Added the ability to cancel ladder spawning.[/h3] 
Simply click the pickup button (RMB) while holding the spawn button (LMB). 
[*][h3]Camera view reset when player moves[/h3]
Now, when the player moves after zooming out the camera, the camera returns to its default position.
[*][h3]Changed spawn and initial obstacles on the hard level.[/h3]
[*][h3]Added an extra rock in the narrow passage at the beginning so players don't get stuck between them[/h3]
Even if it didn't affect gameplay that much (you could always jump out from it) it could make player confused.
[*][h3]Fixed a bug that didn't reset death in lava on game restart or going back to menu.[/h3]
[/list]

And that's all for now. Remember to report any bugs, issues, or suggestions via the Steam discussion. When I return, I'll set up a Discord for those who prefer live communication.

Thank you once again to everyone who purchased the game, and keep laddering up!

notes.title: Ladder It Up! - Update #1 | Ladder Spawn fix, Ladder highlight and more
notes.notes:
The first update is coming out today and includes the following fixes:

[list]

[*][h3]Improved ladder spawn system[/h3] The ladder will no longer perform tricks like a skateboard when spawned too close to player. Player now blocks ladder spawns. Ladder should no longer spawn inside or behind walls (there were a few such spots. Thanks Plami).

[*][h3]Added a highlight for the ladder when it is far from the player.[/h3]  This will help locate it in dark areas like the Crystal Cave.

[*][h3]Added a "Restart" label next to the game reset button.[/h3]

[*][h3]Improved lighting in the Lava Cave.[/h3]

[*][h3]Fixed a bug that caused the ladder to spawn after clicking on the menu screen.[/h3]

[/list]

And that's all for today. Report any bugs, and they will be fixed next week due to the trip I mentioned in my previous post. Additionally, I want to thank everyone who purchased Ladder It Up! You are awesome and keep climbing!
